A1.justification: Both PDFs describe ViT-Linearizer and provide readable main text, equations, three figures, nine tables, and Appendix A. Their complete contents support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original classification, semantic segmentation, efficiency, and ablation results in Section 4, Tables 1–6, and Figure 3.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experimental results, including the distilled models' benchmark performance and component ablations.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the same frozen ViT teacher, Adventurer student, activation matching over visible tokens, masked prediction, and combined loss. No algorithmic component or procedure changes.

E1.justification: Both versions distill on ImageNet-1k and evaluate ImageNet classification and ADE20K/Cityscapes semantic segmentation. No dataset, task, or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Tables 1–4 retain their respective comparator and teacher sets, including CLIP, MAE, DeiT/DeiT-III, Vim, and supervised Adventurer where originally reported. The additional citations do not introduce evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Input resolutions, model configurations, accuracy and mIoU metrics, throughput measurement, and training budgets remain unchanged. This includes encoder-only segmentation timing and the schedules in Appendix Tables 8–9.

E4.justification: The teacher-source and student-size studies, component ablations, masking comparisons, and activation-matching variants in Tables 4–6 are unchanged. Figure 3 retains the same qualitative activation-map examples.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The statistical reporting practice is unchanged throughout the main text and appendix.

E6.justification: All corresponding result entries and findings are retained. For example, the distilled Adventurer-Base still achieves 84.3% ImageNet accuracy at 224×224, 51.3% ADE20K mIoU, and 82.0% Cityscapes mIoU in Tables 1–3.

T1.justification: Equations 1–6, the activation-map and loss definitions, and the quadratic-versus-linear complexity reasoning are unchanged. No formal assumptions, derivations, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: transferring ViT knowledge into linear-time recurrent models through activation matching and masked prediction, with favorable accuracy-efficiency trade-offs. Small wording edits do not alter these claims.

C2.justification: Both versions retain the same explanations concerning sharper activations, information leakage from matching masked tokens, and distillation across teacher/student sizes. The discussion of manageable experimental scales and future larger-scale exploration is also unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix A retains the same architecture configurations and optimization, augmentation, and fine-tuning settings in Tables 7–9. Hardware and measurement details are unchanged, and no code or data access instructions are added.

R1.justification: v2 adds four cited works: Autoregressive Pretraining with Mamba in Vision, M-VAR, FlowAR, and Learning to Decompose Visual Features with Latent Textual Prompts. These supplement existing citation groups in Sections 1–2; all earlier references and the substantive positioning argument remain.

P1.justification: v2 makes limited grammatical and wording edits, capitalizes Chellappa correctly, and replaces the displayed author email with location information. The narrative and section order remain intact; the abstract also introduces the typo 'performence'.

P2.justification: The author block is reformatted, Table 6 moves from the left to the right column on page 8, and text and references reflow. The unchanged acknowledgements move to page 9. All figures and tables retain their substantive visual content and structure.

improvement.justification: v2 adds a few citations and makes small editorial corrections, while also introducing the abstract typo 'performence'. These limited adjustments and layout shifts do not meaningfully improve or harm the paper's overall quality; its method, supporting evidence, interpretations, and appendix reproducibility information remain unchanged.
